Fixture: the rule no-absolute-home-path in .github/invariants.txt has to match
nothing in this file.

Each line below is the legal way to write the line above it in the refused
fixture, and each sits close enough to it that a rule written slightly too wide
would take it. A rule that refuses the correct spelling beside the violation is
a rule whoever meets it turns off, and then it refuses nothing at all.

    %USERPROFILE%\src\reissbrett\notes.md
    $HOME/src/reissbrett/notes.md
    ~/src/reissbrett/notes.md
    /usr/local/share/reissbrett/notes.md
    ./docs/decisions/0005-the-pinned-suite-version.md

The last two are the ones worth having. An absolute path that is not somebody's
home directory is legal, and so is a path relative to the repository root, and a
rule reaching for either would be red on the day it landed.

Two more spellings that carry the word without carrying a path: the home
directories live under /home on Linux and under /Users on macOS, and neither of
those is followed by an account name here.
